summary: Reserved pool throughput collapse during low-traffic window caused by tenant background training job and autoscale mis-sizing
description:
Issue summary:
Customers observed a sudden drop in throughput and a spike in p95/p99 latency for requests routed to NimbusAI's reserved GPU pool during an off-peak window (approx 02:10 - 02:45 UTC). Requests returned 504s and streaming connections frequently reset.

Impact:
- NimbusAI (dedicated) reports 40-70% reduction in sustained token/sec for long-sequence inference (seq > 1024).
- Several production endpoints experienced request timeouts and retries, causing downstream rate-limiter escalations.

Environment:
- Dedicated reserved pool: prod-us-east (reservation id: rsv-78c2)
- Autoscaler policy: min_replicas=2, target_util=0.7, cooldown=300s (recently adjusted on 2026-03-08)
- Models: gptx-13b (quantized), gptx-7b

Steps to reproduce (as performed by Support/SRE):
1) Replayed customer traffic pattern (short burst followed by steady long-seq inference) against a staging copy of rsv-78c2.
2) Injected a background training / checkpointing job (tenant-owned) to reproduce memory-swap/VRAM pressure characteristics.
3) Observed scheduler placing small background processes on same GPU nodes as inference pods.

Observed behavior:
- Sudden eviction/restart of inference containers when background job peak occurred.
- Autoscaler did not scale quickly enough due to cooldown+low observed CPU metrics (scheduling pressure was VRAM/paging, not CPU).
- KV-cache thrashing: cache-hit ratio dropped ~30% at the start of the window which amplified per-request latency.

Expected behavior:
- Reserved pool should maintain baseline throughput during off-peak workloads with soft isolation between tenant jobs and inference pods.

Logs/metrics/links:
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/throughput/nimbus-rsv-78c2 (p95/p99, pod restarts)
- SRE trace: https://traces.internal/redwood/trace/0c4f9b
- Kernel logs (node n-usp-12): /var/log/kern-2026-03-10.log (attached)
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: noisy neighbor from tenant background job causing VRAM pressure leading to kernel-level thrashing and OOM-kicks.

SRE findings:
- Node-level dmesg showed repeated GPU page-fault and MIG reclaim messages coincident with increased background IO.
- Pod-level cgroups indicated stable CPU/mem usage for inference pods, but GPU memory allocation spikes and NVidia driver warnings present.
- Autoscaler uses node-level CPU and pod CPU metrics; it did not see the correct signal for GPU memory pressure.

Engineering notes:
- Confirmed autoscale cooldown (300s) plus conservative scale-up policy allowed multiple eviction events before new pods stabilized.
- Scheduler placed background training containers on same GPU nodes due to insufficient node taints/affinity rules for tenant jobs.

Workarounds trialed:
- Temporarily cordoned two nodes and migrated inference pods to fresh nodes (immediate throughput recovery).
- Applied a short-term autoscaler override to force scale to 6 replicas (bypassed cooldown), which reduced tail latency but increased cost.
resolution:
Root cause: combination of tenant background job performing checkpoint/IO heavy work on shared GPU nodes (noisy neighbor) and autoscaler mis-sizing/metric selection that failed to respond to GPU memory pressure.

Fixes applied:
1) Immediate: cordon/migrate affected nodes, forced scale to restore capacity for NimbusAI (completed 2026-03-10 03:10 UTC).
2) Near-term: updated autoscaler to include GPU memory pressure metric and lowered cooldown to 120s for affected dedicated pools (rolled 2026-03-11).
3) Mid-term: introduced node taints and scheduler affinity baseline for reserved pools to avoid co-scheduling tenant training jobs with inference pods; added admission check to flag heavy background workloads.

Customer communication: Notified NimbusAI of root cause and mitigations; provided guidance to avoid scheduling heavy training/checkpointing on reserved inference nodes.

Follow-ups:
- ENG-OPS task to add synthetic GPU-memory load test to CI for autoscaler validation.
- SRE runbook update to include GPU paging indicators and recommended emergency steps.
